description: A fluid-limit approximation may separate average behavior from rare obstruction events. This card compresses the arithmetic state into divisor-profile buckets and fits a Wormald-style drift model that predicts how average gap and record-gap scales should evolve.
mathematical_formalization: Let U_n(\beta) count uncovered integers in bucket \beta, where \beta may encode smoothness, \omega(x), or observed witness multiplicity. Estimate \mathbb{E}[U_{n+1}(\beta)-U_n(\beta)\mid \mathcal{F}_n] \approx F_\beta(U_n/n), derive an ODE or mean-field map, and compare its predicted gap tails with data.
analogical_connections: mean-field limits for greedy graph processes
implementation_hypothesis: Use computed trajectories to fit bucket-level drifts and forecast future gap records. If the fitted model predicts bounded or slowly varying local gaps despite unbounded record times, it clarifies what sort of proof obstruction remains.
experiment_seed: Fit drift models on the first 2000 steps, forecast the next 4000, and compare predicted record-gap counts against the exact simulation.

closest_prior_art.title: The differential equation method for random graph processes and greedy algorithms
The distribution of integers with a divisor in a given interval
Random graphs with arbitrary degree distributions and their applications

novelty_claim: The novelty lies in bucketizing by arithmetic divisor profile rather than generic graph degree, letting the fluid model talk directly to product coverage.
differentiation: This is not a generic random-process fit; the state variables are chosen to preserve the multiplicative geometry of the frontier.
